answer: The paper describes node2vec as running on a single machine rather than a distributed cluster. Its three sequential phases (preprocessing of transition probabilities, random-walk simulation, and SGD optimization of skip-gram embeddings) were parallelized across the cores of one multi-core, shared-memory machine, with the graph held in RAM. The reference implementation is in Python, using Gensim's word2vec-style SGD. I recall the scalability experiments using a 16-core machine with on the order of 60+ GB of RAM, but I am not certain of those exact figures.
